faq.question: What is the best ramen in Chicago?
faq.answer: Akahoshi Ramen is the most consistently recommended on Reddit. Chef Mike Satinover (u/Ramen_Lord) turned a decade of ramen study into Chicago's most hyped shop. Ramen Wasabi and Monster Ramen are close seconds.

faq.question: Where can I get tonkotsu ramen in Chicago?
faq.answer: Ramen Wasabi (Logan Square) is the tonkotsu king with 45-hour broth. Ramen Takeya (Fulton Market) and Rudy's Ramen (Noble Square) also serve excellent tonkotsu.

faq.question: What is the most unique ramen in Chicago?
faq.answer: Monster Ramen uses bison bone (gyukotsu) broth. Oiistar cross-pollinates ramen with tikka masala, mussels, and chipotle. Both are in the Wicker Park/Logan Square area.

faq.question: Is there good ramen on Chicago's south side?
faq.answer: TNT Ramen (8929 S Commercial Ave) is a south side gem with a 4.9 rating. Four focused bowls with housemade noodles, open Wed-Sun.

faq.question: How much does ramen cost in Chicago?
faq.answer: Most bowls range from $14-$19. Add $2-3 for extra toppings. Budget around $18-25 per person including a drink and appetizer.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for Chicago ramen shops?
faq.answer: Only Akahoshi Ramen requires reservations — they book out 5 weeks ahead via OpenTable. All others are walk-in only.

faq.question: What is tantanmen ramen?
faq.answer: Tantanmen is a Japanese adaptation of Sichuan dan dan noodles featuring a nutty, spicy pork broth with Sichuan peppercorns. Menya Goku in North Center specializes in this style.
